reason: Title explicitly states 'hedgehog pathway in lens regeneration' - directly ocular. SMO is the obligate transducer of Hedgehog signaling; a paper on lens (eye) regeneration via this pathway is squarely within SMO's ocular-genetics scope (structural eye disease, microphthalmia, coloboma).
Wide-field OCT and angiography specifically in X-linked retinoschisis. RS1 is the causative gene for XLRS; clinical imaging characterisation of this disease is core to any RS1 gene-specific library.

Scotopic threshold response abnormalities correlated with gene mutations in X-linked retinoschisis. The RS1 gene is explicitly named in the title alongside XLRS phenotype; directly characterises electrophysiological correlates of RS1 mutations.

Paper characterises hypomorphic SMO variants in holoprosencephaly using zebrafish bioassays. Although SMO is central and HPE can in extreme cases involve midline eye anomalies, this paper addresses forebrain/craniofacial midline patterning exclusively and mentions no ocular phenotype. The SMO library entry is justified by coloboma/microphthalmia; a purely HPE-focused study without eye phenotyping does not meet that relevance bar.

Case report of prenatal postaxial polydactyly caused by bi-allelic SMO variants. The abstract and subject are limited to limb digit formation; no eye or craniofacial phenotype is described. Does not connect to the ocular-structural-disease rationale for tracking SMO.

Pallister-Hall-Like Syndrome with homozygous SMO variant. Clinical features listed are postaxial polydactyly, hypothalamic hamartoma, cardiac/skeletal anomalies, and craniofacial dysmorphism; no ocular phenotype is reported. Without an eye-disease link this falls outside the ophthalmogenetics scope of the SMO collection.

Case report demonstrating ROCK inhibitor (ripasudil) resolving retinoschisis and cystic foveal cavities in X-linked retinoschisis. RS1-disease treatment study with OCT documentation; directly relevant to RS1 clinical management literature.

Novel SMO missense variant causing isolated autosomal-recessive postaxial polydactyly in two consanguineous families. Entirely focused on digit/limb development via the Sonic Hedgehog pathway; no eye phenotype is mentioned. Does not satisfy the ocular-structural-disease criterion for the SMO collection.

Investigates Na-Ca exchange current in isolated rod outer segments - exactly the physiological function of SLC24A1 (NCKX1, the rod photoreceptor Na+/Ca2+-K+ exchanger). This is a foundational electrophysiology paper on the protein product of SLC24A1 in its native retinal compartment; directly relevant to the CSNB1D/retinal-dystrophy focus of the SLC24A1 collection.

Clinical review of idiopathic infantile nystagmus diagnosis and treatment. FRMD7 is the causative gene for X-linked idiopathic congenital nystagmus (NYS1); clinical management literature on the phenotype is core to the FRMD7 collection even when the gene is not named in the title.

Cohort study of X-linked retinoschisis clinical presentations in Taiwanese patients with RS1 gene sequencing confirming diagnosis and identifying nine mutations including six novel ones. Directly characterises RS1 genotype-phenotype relationships.

Hereditary study of congenital nystagmus in a Swedish population. FRMD7 mutations are the principal cause of X-linked hereditary congenital nystagmus; population-level hereditary genetics of this phenotype is directly within scope for the FRMD7 collection, even as a pre-molecular era paper establishing inheritance patterns.
